p4_card.identity: A class-level comparison of interventions on one need (postsynaptic excitatory gain and bursting in the neuron-specific Wwox knockout cortex). Classes: (A) complete competitive glutamate-site block: d-APV, a tool and the only NMDAR agent applied in a WWOX system, and selfotel, a clinical-stage relative stopped in adult stroke and head-injury trials; (B) use-dependent pore blockers: memantine and ketamine (approved in adults), dextromethorphan, amantadine, dizocilpine (tool); (C) subunit-selective negative allosteric modulators: GluN2B (tools Ro 25-6981 and ifenprodil; radiprodil, clinical stage in GRIN gain-of-function disease and other registrations), GluN2A (tools TCN-201, NVP-AAM077) and GluN2C/2D (tool NAB-14); (E) glycine-site agents (tools L-701,324 and 7-chlorokynurenic acid; D-cycloserine, an approved antibiotic with partial-agonist action); (F) AMPAR: perampanel (approved), NBQX and GYKI 52466 (tools). A compound named here is an identity, not a recommendation, and an effect of a tool compound is not the effect of a different drug.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: Only IF the bursting depends on an NMDAR contribution that a partial, subunit-restricted or use-dependent action can lower without the cost of a complete block in a developing brain. The d-APV result fits three readings that predict different things: NMDAR gain (more NMDAR current per synapse), permissive necessity (normal NMDARs that the network recruits because the pyramidal neurons are depolarised and inhibition is reduced) and an AMPAR-led drive. No receptor-level measurement exists in any WWOX system. Transfer to the reference genotype is unmeasured: the slice is a neuron-specific knockout, not an allele.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: F01 (2026-10-27) registered a graded memantine versus perampanel versus d-APV experiment. This card keeps F01 intact and supersedes its discriminator, on four findings of 2026-10-29: (1) block by memantine and ketamine depends on extracellular Mg2+ (nearly twenty-fold weaker at GluN2A and GluN2B but about three-fold at GluN2C and GluN2D, abstract level) and on intracellular Ca2+ (GluN2A); the preparation held 1.3 millimolar Mg2+ in its incubation solution, so a memantine result there may reflect GluN2D-containing interneurons rather than pyramidal GluN2A/2B receptors; (2) the knockout pyramidal neurons are about five millivolts depolarised and receive fewer and smaller inhibitory currents, which can produce NMDAR-dependent bursting with a normal receptor; (3) a GluN2B-selective NAM has a ceiling below complete inhibition, a clinical-stage member with human exposure (adults, three infants, registered paediatric studies) and a rat-pup age of largest protection (no species age mapping to the mouse window is established); (4) the baseline burst rate is low and is reported twice with different values (about two per minute in the main text, below one per minute in the supplementary table, for bursts the main text does not count, an inference that they are the same bursts), so a graded block read from bursts alone needs long recordings per condition and should be backed by a faster NMDAR readout in the same slices. Coverage: PubMed and Europe PMC, ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, ChEMBL_37 and openFDA on 2026-10-29; NON_TROVATO_NELLA_RICERCA for any GluN2B NAM, pore blocker, glycine-site agent or AMPAR antagonist other than d-APV in a Wwox system, not MAI_TENTATO.
p4_card.state_of_known_roads: F01; map R-02 and Chain B; N-15 (seizure or burst control is not development); DL-MECH-002; F02 (activity-dependent myelination) and F03 (chloride gradient, a depolarisation and inhibition lever) as the upstream alternatives if the NMDAR dependence proves permissive.
p4_card.pathway_and_objective: BENEFICIO_PRECOCE; Track A; Track B untested.
p4_card.expected_contribution: UNKNOWN. At best the receptor-level fact that decides whether an NMDAR-class intervention is a lever (partial block suffices) or only a symptom tool (near-complete block needed); no developmental benefit is implied.
p4_card.mechanism: Targets: NMDAR (GRIN1 with GRIN2A, GRIN2B and GRIN2D; GRIN2C untested) and AMPAR (GRIA1 to GRIA4). Direction wanted: lower excitatory gain. The classes act on different receptor states: competitive and glycine-site agents on the agonist-bound receptor irrespective of voltage; pore blockers only on open channels, with voltage, Mg2+ and Ca2+ dependence; negative allosteric modulators lower open probability, some incompletely, and depend on co-agonist level or pH; AMPAR antagonists remove the depolarisation that relieves the Mg2+ block, so an AMPAR result cannot isolate the NMDAR.

for: d-APV abolishes bursting in the knockout slice, and the delayed evoked response is d-APV-sensitive at higher stimulus strengths.

Excitatory current amplitude is slightly higher in the knockout (sEPSC means 24.7 against 23.3 pA, about six percent, pooled-event tests; the mEPSC panel separates by a sliver); recorded at -70 mV in Mg2+, so AMPAR-weighted.

A GluN2B-selective NAM is effective at most tested gain-of-function GRIN variants in vitro and in a gain-of-function knock-in mouse (abstract); memantine improvement in any domain in a GRIN series is concentrated in gain-of-function variants (mainly behaviour; seizure-frequency reduction was not significantly different).
against: NMDAR dependence is not NMDAR gain: depolarised resting potential and reduced inhibition suffice (not tested). The largest synaptic change in the source is inhibitory (sIPSC amplitude 27.5 against 57.3 pA in controls, frequency also reduced), not excitatory.
The d-APV arm carries no significance marker in Fig 3D, n 5 slices from 3 animals, and the paper tests bursts (51), not animals.
The bursting is cortical; hippocampal slices of the same mice do not burst.

A competitive full-block antagonist (selfotel) failed with a harm signal in adults; NMDAR blockade in the developing rat brain triggers apoptosis (abstract level); memantine has no paediatric effectiveness on its label.

Potency tables are heterogeneous: voltage, Mg2+, Ca2+, glycine, assay type and species change the number by orders of magnitude, row counts overstate independence, and subunit selectivity is assay-conditional.
Every clinical-stage GluN2B NAM study is in gain-of-function GRIN disease, where the sign is known; WWOX has no receptor-level datum.
evidence_for_and_against.transfer_limits: Juvenile slice, one laboratory, knockout not allele; recording solution not separately stated; an acute slice experiment cannot say anything about chronic block and activity-dependent maturation (F02).

p4_card.time_to_access: Memantine, ketamine, perampanel and D-cycloserine are marketed under adult or other labels; radiprodil is investigational (registered studies only); tool compounds are research reagents. Access for a WWOX study: UNKNOWN.
p4_card.pharmacology: Potency values are in the cycle README and TSV tables, not here. They come from heterogeneous assays (oocyte voltage clamp, HEK or CHO flux, membrane binding, review transcriptions); a median across them describes the literature, not a drug property. One value is repeated across many documents (eliprodil at GluN2B, ketamine in a review document), and target organism and assay organism differ or are blank in many rows. The receptor state (open, desensitised, agonist and co-agonist level, voltage, Mg2+) is not a ChEMBL field and had to be read from assay text or documents.
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: Memantine label: paediatric safety and effectiveness not established; two controlled paediatric autism studies failed. Perampanel label: partial-onset seizures from 4 years of age; boxed warning for serious psychiatric and behavioural reactions. Radiprodil: investigational; registered paediatric studies are in GRIN gain-of-function disease and TSC or FCD; two of them (the GRIN phase 1b and the TSC / FCD study) exclude co-administered glutamate-receptor agonists or antagonists (memantine, perampanel and felbamate named), the phase 3 posted text does not. Developing-brain NMDAR blockade: apoptotic neurodegeneration in rat pups (abstract). Other interactions: UNKNOWN.

Abstract only: Kotermanski 2009, Banke 2026, Ikonomidou 1999, the selfotel trials, a memantine-in-epilepsy cohort, SUPER-CAT, the source paper of document CHEMBL6083260. p4_card.predictions: Proposed before any experiment; criteria, cut-offs and the smallest effect size are to be written and time-stamped by the laboratory before unblinding. The three readings are not ranked and are not exclusive; the isolated NMDAR current decides between them, the pharmacology is exploratory. (1) If the isolated NMDAR-mediated current is larger in the knockout than in wild type and heterozygote, an NMDAR gain component is present and the GRIN gain-of-function precedents become relevant; a GluN2B-selective NAM concentration-response then says how much of that current must be blocked, defined only if bursts are abolished at its plateau (otherwise the result is persistence at the plateau fraction). (2) If the isolated NMDAR current is not raised, the dependence is permissive: no receptor change is needed to explain it, NMDAR block is a symptom tool whose window is read from the pharmacology, and the upstream levers (resting potential, inhibition) become the mechanism-matched ones. (3) If wild-type slices made to burst by a matched trigger respond to the same blocks with the same concentration-response, the dependence is generic to NMDAR-driven networks and is not a WWOX-specific finding. (4) An AMPAR antagonist abolishing bursts is expected under every reading and does not separate them. A permissive result (2) or a generic result (3) closes the NMDAR-lever strand without closing the symptom-tool use.
p4_card.next_measurement: Wet-lab, not done. Preparation as in the source (neuron-specific knockout with littermate wild type and heterozygote, postnatal day 13 to 17, both sexes, coronal slices, the source's incubation solution, layer II/III recording, burst inclusion criterion as in the source). Unit: the animal, with slices and cells nested (the source tested bursts and cells). In the same slices: (a) NMDAR-isolated current under voltage control with AMPAR and GABA-A blocked, amplitude, decay and the fraction sensitive to a GluN2B NAM and to a GluN2A NAM, plus resting potential and input resistance; (b) concentration-response of d-APV and of a GluN2B-selective NAM tool on the isolated current and on the delayed evoked response, then on bursts, to measure the fraction of NMDAR current that must be blocked to stop bursting; (c) a use-dependent pore blocker with the Mg2+ level and voltage reported, as a translation probe after (a) and (b); (d) wild-type slices made to burst by a matched trigger with the same pharmacology; (e) a time-matched vehicle arm and washout. Counting time: for about twenty percent precision on a rate (25 bursts) a condition needs about eleven minutes at the main-text rate and about half an hour at the supplementary-table rate; the discrepancy between the two reported baselines must be resolved first.
p4_card.value_added: Turns the d-APV result from a yes-or-no into a question with a measurable answer (the fraction of NMDAR current that must be blocked), names the alternative readings that the record had not separated (depolarisation, reduced inhibition, AMPAR drive), and replaces memantine as the discriminating arm with a class whose interpretation does not depend on Mg2+, voltage and Ca2+.
p4_card.clinical_census: ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-29: a radiprodil query returned ten registrations (paediatric GRIN gain-of-function, TSC and focal cortical dysplasia, infantile spasms, adult pharmacology); none in WWOX. The WWOX census of 2026-10-20 is unchanged and was not re-run. One registry, one date, a missing hit does not prove absence.

not_known: Whether NMDAR current, subunit composition or surface level is raised in any WWOX system.
The fraction of NMDAR current that must be blocked to stop bursting.
Whether the dependence is generic to NMDAR-driven networks or specific to the knockout.
Whether the raised mEPSC amplitude is AMPAR-mediated and whether AMPAR block is necessary for bursting.
The recording solution Mg2+ concentration (only the incubation solution is stated).
Whether any partial, subunit-selective or use-dependent block reproduces the effect of the full block.
Whether any such block affects maturation in a developing Wwox-deficient brain.
evidence_against: NMDAR dependence is not NMDAR gain: depolarised resting potential and reduced inhibition suffice (not tested). The largest synaptic change in the source is inhibitory (sIPSC amplitude 27.5 against 57.3 pA in controls, frequency also reduced), not excitatory.
The d-APV arm carries no significance marker in Fig 3D, n 5 slices from 3 animals, and the paper tests bursts (51), not animals.
The bursting is cortical; hippocampal slices of the same mice do not burst.

A competitive full-block antagonist (selfotel) failed with a harm signal in adults; NMDAR blockade in the developing rat brain triggers apoptosis (abstract level); memantine has no paediatric effectiveness on its label.

Potency tables are heterogeneous: voltage, Mg2+, Ca2+, glycine, assay type and species change the number by orders of magnitude, row counts overstate independence, and subunit selectivity is assay-conditional.
Every clinical-stage GluN2B NAM study is in gain-of-function GRIN disease, where the sign is known; WWOX has no receptor-level datum.
bridge_gaps_exposed: d-APV is carried by F01 only; this card carries no assertion on d-APV, so the bridge forms no sign comparison against the disease rows of this card.
Class and tool rows share the target but differ in block type, state, voltage and Mg2+ dependence; no comparison across classes is formed.
GRIN and registry rows are other diseases; no sign is compared with the slice rows.

translation.pediatric_suitability: Memantine: not established on its label. Perampanel: labelled from 4 years of age for partial-onset seizures. Radiprodil: investigational. WWOX-DEE: UNKNOWN.

p4_roadmap_fields.indication_and_transfer: Only IF the bursting depends on an NMDAR contribution that a partial, subunit-restricted or use-dependent action can lower without the cost of a complete block in a developing brain. The d-APV result fits three readings that predict different things: NMDAR gain (more NMDAR current per synapse), permissive necessity (normal NMDARs that the network recruits because the pyramidal neurons are depolarised and inhibition is reduced) and an AMPAR-led drive. No receptor-level measurement exists in any WWOX system. Transfer to the reference genotype is unmeasured: the slice is a neuron-specific knockout, not an allele.

card_conventions: IPOTESI throughout; the bridge forces it. No score, rank, probability or blended index is carried.
directional_summary compares signs only where target, endpoint and every context dimension match; UNRESOLVED is a statement about the record, not about the biology.

Association is not modulation is not rescue; an effect of a tool compound is not the effect of a different drug.
